title: Getting Married in the Dominican Republic: Documents
seoTitle: Getting Married in the Dominican Republic: Documents
description: Organize documents for a civil wedding in the Dominican Republic: registrar review, foreign records, apostille or legalization, translation and certificate follow-up.
directAnswer: Start with the Dominican civil registry office that will handle your marriage and request a checklist for both partners' nationalities, residence and marital histories. Identity, birth and civil-status documents are central, with additional records where applicable. Confirm authentication, Spanish translation, original-document requirements and deadlines before ordering or translating anything. A hotel checklist does not replace the registrar's review.

sections.heading: Identify the authority and the exact legal event
paragraphs: Determine whether you are arranging a Dominican civil marriage or a symbolic celebration after marrying elsewhere. The paperwork differs fundamentally. A venue may offer both events under similar wedding-package names, so ask which service the proposal actually includes and who arranges the civil official.

For a civil marriage, identify the competent Oficialía del Estado Civil and obtain its current instructions for your case. Give both partners' nationalities, residence, place of birth and relevant marital history. Do not rely on the document list of friends whose nationality or circumstances differ.

sections.heading: Use the official checklist as the starting point
paragraphs: The JCE lists identity and birth records, applicable divorce documentation and at least two adult witnesses with identification. Its guidance also addresses foreign civil-status evidence and translation. Treat the list as the starting point for a case-specific confirmation, not permission to omit an item that the receiving office requests.

sources.label: JCE: requirements for a civil marriage

sections.heading: Create one document tracker for each partner
paragraphs: Record the document name, issuing country, issuing authority, requested version, issue date, authentication route, translation status and person reviewing it. Add separate columns for originals, copies and delivery. This prevents an apparently complete folder from hiding a missing authentication or an unacceptable version.

Use the names exactly as shown on the documents. Flag differences in surnames, transliteration, birth dates or place names early. Ask the receiving office how to resolve discrepancies before paying to translate a document that may need correction or replacement.

sections.heading: Understand authentication before arranging translation
paragraphs: Ask whether each foreign document needs an apostille or another legalization route and which authority performs that step in the issuing country. An apostille and a translation serve different purposes; neither should be treated as a substitute for the other. Confirm the required sequence rather than guessing from an online checklist.

Ask who may provide an accepted Spanish translation and whether that translation needs additional certification. A hotel's bilingual coordinator or an informal translation may help communication but does not automatically satisfy official documentary requirements. Request a written answer identifying the accepted procedure for your documents.

sections.heading: Handle previous marriages and special circumstances early
paragraphs: Tell the receiving authority about any previous marriage, divorce or bereavement before the final checklist is issued. Ask which records demonstrate your current legal status and whether the underlying decision or only a civil-register document is required. Do not assume a foreign document's title has an exact Dominican equivalent.

If you intend a particular matrimonial property arrangement, obtain qualified advice before setting document deadlines. That is a separate legal decision, not a decorative option in a wedding package. Similarly, direct questions about eligibility or unresolved civil records to the competent authority rather than asking an event supplier to interpret them.

sections.heading: Separate official deadlines from hotel deadlines
paragraphs: A resort may request scans weeks before the event or set an arrival requirement for operational reasons. Ask which dates come from the civil registry and which are the hotel's processing rules. Both can affect your plan, but they should not be described as the same legal requirement.

Build the schedule backward from the registrar's review: issuing records, authentication, translation, correction if necessary, delivery and final confirmation. Do not publish a universal document-validity period or waiting time without confirmation for the relevant office and current procedure. Leave a practical buffer for reissued records.

sections.heading: Agree who submits, carries and returns the documents
paragraphs: Name the person responsible for each handoff. Ask whether the office will review scans before originals arrive and whether the person submitting them needs authorization. Record where originals will be kept, when they will be returned and who can answer a last-minute query.

Carry the documents in the way agreed with the receiving office and keep a secure backup of the submitted version. Avoid sending passport copies into general wedding-group chats. A décor vendor or musician does not need the couple's complete legal file to perform an event service.

sections.heading: Budget for the process rather than one advertised fee
paragraphs: Request separate amounts for official fees, document issuance, authentication, accepted translation, courier services and any coordination assistance. Confirm currencies and payment methods. Ask whether a quoted wedding-package fee includes the actual civil service or only the symbolic ceremony.

Do not assume that an old consular fee, a resort supplement or another couple's invoice is your final total. Different services may be performed by different authorities. A complete estimate should identify the provider and scope of every charge so you can distinguish official payments from private administrative support.

sections.heading: Plan certificate collection and use abroad
paragraphs: Before the wedding, ask how the marriage will be registered and how you obtain the official certificate. Confirm who collects it, the delivery address, the procedure if you have already left the country and how an error is corrected. A commemorative ceremony document should not be mistaken for the civil record.

Then contact the authority in the country where the certificate will be used. Ask whether additional authentication, translation, registration or transcription is required. The requirements for marrying in the Dominican Republic and using the resulting certificate abroad are separate tasks; completing the first does not automatically complete the second.

sections.heading: Keep the event plan workable while documents are reviewed
paragraphs: Track the legal process separately from catering, transport and décor decisions. Let the planner know only the status and dates needed to coordinate the ceremony. If the official review reveals a delay, review contractual options promptly rather than assuming the ceremony can simply proceed as a legal marriage.

Sertuin Events can coordinate event logistics alongside the documentary process. Bring the confirmed checklist, responsible registrar and relevant deadlines to the planning meeting so the operational schedule reflects what the authorities have actually accepted.

faqs.question: Does a hotel checklist replace the civil registry checklist?
faqs.answer: No. Confirm requirements with the office handling the marriage and distinguish official requirements from the hotel's administrative deadlines.

faqs.question: Can we use our own translation?
faqs.answer: Ask the receiving office which translator and certification procedure it accepts. A bilingual friend or supplier is not automatically an approved translator.

faqs.question: Must every foreign document be apostilled?
faqs.answer: Confirm the appropriate authentication route for each document and issuing country. Do not assume that the same route applies to every record.

faqs.question: Will we receive the official certificate before flying home?
faqs.answer: Obtain a specific collection and delivery plan from the responsible office. Do not assume issuance will match your departure date.

faqs.question: Does a symbolic wedding require this legal file?
faqs.answer: A purely symbolic event does not itself create the civil marriage. Any separate legal marriage must follow the requirements of the authority conducting it.

ctaTitle: Coordinate your wedding around confirmed requirements
ctaText: Share the registrar's confirmed deadlines and your event plans to organize the Punta Cana celebration.
